fit: brewed lemon balm and depression in hospitalized burn patients
assessment: The retrospective trial IRCT201205198177N4 specifies Beck depression and black tea. The no-depression category rose under lemon balm. Prior depression was excluded and the paper describes replacement after early discharge. The published severity comparison remains ambiguous.

fit: lemon balm extract capsules and Beck depression scores in type 2 diabetes
assessment: Of 60 randomized, 44 completed. Table 4 shows BDI-II change −3.91 versus −0.04 and similar final means with higher extract baseline. Adjusted p=.001. Trial length differs between Methods and table caption. Extract capsules and type 2 diabetes limit transfer.

fit: lemon balm anise rose capsules and depression in IBS
assessment: The paper identifies IRCT20150927024228N4. The reported HADS depression interval crosses zero and is asymmetric around its labeled estimate. The matched gastrointestinal report provides separate outcomes of the likely same cohort. Neither paper isolates lemon balm.

fit: same egg isolate with or without dried-leaf-derived lemon balm
assessment: Adding dried-leaf-derived lemon balm yields HAM-D improvement of 8.4 versus 10.1 points with egg alone, and BDI-II improvement of 11.0 versus 10.5. The active arms do not differ significantly. Neither numerical contrast supplies a reliable brewed-tea effect.

fit: confirmed brewed tea and rose crossover with distinct unresolved depression endpoint
assessment: The full original confirms this ID and reports 20 residents with a one-week washout. Its verified anxiety result under tea is 16.85 (SD 2.46). Methods name BDI and describe anxiety scoring. No separate depression estimate is reported. The 2024 abstract family remains provisional.
